edges.description: The cerebellar syndrome progresses to loss of independent walking, with the axonal neuropathy adding to the same disability.
The neuropathy compounds the cerebellar disability rather than causing loss of walking on its own.
Reproduces the oxidative damage, double-strand break burden, R-loop accumulation and damage-induced cell death of AOA2 in a human neural cell type.
edges.limitations: Neural progenitors are proliferating cells, so they do not answer the question the mouse data raised about whether the same phenotype occurs in post-mitotic neurons; and the system rests on a single patient line and a single control.

edges.description: Complete loss of Setx in the mouse produces no cerebellar degeneration and no ataxia, so the model cannot be used to study the neurodegenerative arm of AOA2.
edges.limitations: The negative result is not a matter of degree or of age at assessment: neither structural cerebellar change nor Purkinje cell loss was detectable, and behavioural scoring found no difference from wild type. Any inference about AOA2 neurodegeneration made in this model is therefore unsupported, which is why patient-derived iPSC neural progenitors were developed instead.

edges.description: R-loops accumulate in Setx-null tissue, but only where cells are proliferating. The brain of the same animals shows none.
edges.limitations: The tissue restriction is the whole point: R-loop accumulation was demonstrated in testis and in proliferating cells in vitro and in vivo, and was absent from the brains of Setx-null mice. A model of R-loop accumulation in this system is a model of a proliferating-cell phenomenon, and cannot be transferred to post-mitotic neurons.
edges.target: Defective R-Loop Resolution at Transcription Pause Sites

edges.description: An AFP above the 7 microg/l threshold in an ataxic patient is what selects SETX for sequencing. The link is empirical: no mechanism connecting senataxin loss to AFP production has been established, so this is recorded as a correlation with the genetic lesion rather than as a readout of any modelled mechanism node.

nodes.description: Neural progenitors differentiated from iPSCs reprogrammed from an AOA2 patient's fibroblasts, with a control line. Built specifically because the knockout mouse does not degenerate, this is currently the only neuronal system in which the AOA2 cellular phenotype has been shown.

evidence.reference_title: A new model to study neurodegeneration in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: To develop a more relevant neuronal model to study neurodegeneration in AOA2, we derived neural progenitors from a patient with AOA2 and a control by induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) reprogramming of fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Double-strand breaks arising at transcription-replication collisions and after oxidative insult are rejoined slowly, and the burden is measurable in patient-derived cells including iPSC-derived neural progenitors.
nodes.id: Accumulation of Unrepaired DNA Double-Strand Breaks

evidence.reference_title: A new model to study neurodegeneration in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: AOA2 iPSC and neural progenitors exhibit increased levels of oxidative damage, DNA double-strand breaks, increased DNA damage-induced cell death and R-loop accumulation.

experimental_models.description: Reproduces the oxidative damage, double-strand break burden, R-loop accumulation and damage-induced cell death of AOA2 in a human neural cell type.
experimental_models.name: AOA2 patient iPSC-derived neural progenitors

nodes.description: Tendon reflexes are lost early, before the neuropathy is clinically severe.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of Spermatogenesis and Infertility in Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2 (AOA2).
evidence.snippet: The major clinical features of AOA2 include onset in the second decade, progressive cerebellar ataxia with axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy, diffuse cerebellar atrophy, frequent oculomotor apraxia, early loss of reflexes, loss of Purkinje cells in the cerebellar cortex, and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) serum level

nodes.description: Speech-recognition software and adapted keyboards compensate for reading difficulty caused by the oculomotor disorder and for writing difficulty caused by upper-limb ataxia. Oculographic study of reading in AOA2 supports the specific framing: reading fails because saccadic intrusions and nystagmus disturb the reading scan, not because lexical-semantic processing is impaired, so the intervention should target the oculomotor bottleneck.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2.
evidence.snippet: Treatment of manifestations: Physical therapy for disabilities resulting from peripheral neuropathy; wheelchair for mobility as needed; educational support (e.g., computer with speech recognition and special keyboard for typing) to compensate for difficulties in reading (caused by oculomotor apraxia) and in writing (caused by upper-limb ataxia).

evidence.reference_title: Oculomotor deficits affect neuropsychological performance in oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: The preservation of lexical-semantic processes confirmed that the reading disability was caused by oculomotor deficits, not cognitive problems.

nodes.description: A severe axonal polyneuropathy affecting sensory and motor fibres, present in essentially all patients and the main driver of disability alongside the ataxia. It is absent in a small number of reported patients, so its absence does not exclude the diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: clinical, biological and genotype/phenotype correlation study of a cohort of 90 patients.
evidence.snippet: Polyneuropathy was found in 97.5% of AOA2 patients, cerebellar atrophy in 96%, occasional oculomotor apraxia in 51%, pyramidal signs in 20.5%, head tremor in 14%, dystonia in 13.5%, strabismus in 12.3% and chorea in 9.5%.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: a clinical, pathologic, and genetic study.
evidence.snippet: High serum AFP levels, motor and sensory axonal neuropathy, and marked cerebellar atrophy on MRI were detected in all the patients who underwent these examinations.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2.
evidence.snippet: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2 (AOA2) is characterized by onset of ataxia between age three and 30 years after initial normal development, axonal sensorimotor neuropathy, oculomotor apraxia, cerebellar atrophy, and elevated serum concentration of alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).

nodes.description: Two loss-of-function SETX alleles, homozygous or compound heterozygous. The reported spectrum is dominated by missense, frameshift and nonsense changes, with a large minority causing premature termination of the 2,677-residue protein; whole-exon deletions and duplications also occur and are missed by sequencing alone, so a convincing phenotype with a single point mutation should prompt dosage analysis.

evidence.reference_title: Senataxin, the ortholog of a yeast RNA helicase, is mutant in ataxia-ocular apraxia 2.
evidence.snippet: We have now identified causative mutations in 15 families, which allows us to clinically define this entity by onset between 10 and 22 years, cerebellar atrophy, axonal sensorimotor neuropathy, oculomotor apraxia and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterisation of a large senataxin (SETX) gene duplication in ataxia with ocular apraxia type 2 (AOA2).
evidence.snippet: Further analysis revealed a large out-of-frame tandem duplication, encompassing exons 7, 8, 9 and 10.

nodes.description: Autophagic flux stalls, ubiquitinated proteins and aggregates accumulate, and mitochondrial defects appear. The same perturbation is present in AOA2 patient fibroblasts, not only in knockdown lines, which is what makes it a disease mechanism rather than an artefact of depletion.
nodes.id: Blocked Autophagic Clearance of Damaged Proteins and Organelles

evidence.reference_title: SETX (senataxin), the helicase mutated in AOA2 and ALS4, functions in autophagy regulation.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of AOA2 patient fibroblasts also revealed a perturbation of the autophagy pathway.

nodes.description: Volume loss in the cerebellum, visible on MRI in essentially every patient. It is not a late marker of severity: it is present in the youngest and most mildly affected patients, and appears to be established at or before symptom onset rather than tracking with disease duration.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: clinical, biological and genotype/phenotype correlation study of a cohort of 90 patients.
evidence.snippet: An increased AFP level as well as cerebellar atrophy seem to be stable in the course of the disease and to occur mostly at or before the onset of the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: a clinical and genetic study of 19 patients.
evidence.snippet: Cerebellar atrophy was more severe in the eldest patients; however it may also be an early sign since it was present in the youngest and paucisymptomatic patients.

nodes.description: The convergence point of the molecular arms: unrepaired breaks, stalled autophagic clearance and a mis-set transcriptional program in cells that cannot dilute damage by dividing. This node is where the mechanism is weakest in human evidence, and the entry says so rather than asserting a clean handover — the neuronal read-out comes from patient iPSC-derived progenitors and from the clinical and neuropathological endpoint, not from affected human brain.
nodes.id: Chronic Genomic and Proteostatic Stress in Post-Mitotic Neurons

evidence.reference_title: A new model to study neurodegeneration in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: Recent evidence suggests that the protein defective in this syndrome, senataxin (SETX), functions in RNA processing to protect the integrity of the genome.

nodes.description: R-loops form behind elongating RNA polymerase II, especially over G-rich pause sites downstream of poly(A) signals, and must be unwound for the transcript to be degraded and the polymerase released. Without senataxin the hybrids persist at these sites and at transcription-replication collision points. Note that the direction of the R-loop change in senataxin-depleted human cells is not uniform across studies, which is recorded as a discussion on this entry rather than smoothed over here.
nodes.id: Defective R-Loop Resolution at Transcription Pause Sites

animal_models.description: R-loops accumulate in Setx-null tissue, but only where cells are proliferating. The brain of the same animals shows none.
animal_models.genotype: Setx knockout (Setx-/-, Cre-LoxP deletion of exon 4)
animal_models.name: Setx knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Human senataxin resolves RNA/DNA hybrids formed at transcriptional pause sites to promote Xrn2-dependent termination.
evidence.snippet: We show that nascent transcripts form RNA/DNA hybrid structures (R-loops) behind elongating Pol II and are especially prevalent over G-rich pause sites positioned downstream of gene poly(A) signals.

nodes.description: Senataxin-depleted cells show read-through past the poly(A) site, reduced polymerase occupancy at affected genes, and altered splice-site selection, consistent with a protein that couples termination to RNA processing through poly(A)-binding proteins.
nodes.id: Defective RNA Polymerase II Transcription Termination

biological_processes: termination of RNA polymerase II transcription

evidence.reference_title: Functional role for senataxin, defective in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2, in transcriptional regulation.
evidence.snippet: RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription termination was defective in cells depleted of senataxin in keeping with the observed interaction of senataxin with poly(A) binding proteins 1 and 2.

evidence.reference_title: Functional role for senataxin, defective in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2, in transcriptional regulation.
evidence.snippet: Binding of RNA polymerase II to candidate genes was significantly reduced in senataxin deficient cells and this was accompanied by decreased transcription of these genes, suggesting a role for senataxin in the regulation/modulation of transcription.

nodes.description: A length-dependent axonal degeneration affecting both sensory and motor fibres. Sural nerve biopsy shows severe depletion of large myelinated fibres, and in at least one patient of small fibres as well. In some patients the sensory component behaves as a ganglionopathy rather than a distal axonopathy, with sensory action potentials lost across all limbs and normal motor conduction.
nodes.id: Degeneration of Sensory and Motor Peripheral Axons

cell_types: sensory neuron of dorsal root ganglion

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: a clinical, pathologic, and genetic study.
evidence.snippet: Sural nerve biopsy revealed a severe depletion of large myelinated fibers in one patient, and both large and small myelinated fibers in another.

evidence.reference_title: Sensory neuronopathy in ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: Taken together, these findings are suggestive of a progressive sensory neuronopathy.

nodes.description: A reproducible set of genes is mis-expressed in AOA2. The signature is detectable in patient fibroblasts, in peripheral blood from members of twelve AOA2 families, and in the cerebellum of Setx knockout mice, and the gene sets affected by AOA2 alleles differ from those affected by ALS4 alleles — which is the strongest available evidence that the two allelic diseases diverge through what senataxin transcribes.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of senataxin alters disease-specific transcriptional networks in patients with ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: To assess this in vivo, we performed gene expression analysis on peripheral blood from members of 12 different AOA2 families and identified an AOA2-specific transcriptional signature.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of senataxin alters disease-specific transcriptional networks in patients with ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: These modules were disease-specific and preserved in patient fibroblasts and in the cerebellum of Setx knockout mice demonstrating conservation across species and cell types, including neurons.

nodes.description: Sumoylated senataxin binds Rrp45, a core subunit of the nuclear RNA exosome, and the two proteins co-localise in nuclear foci at R-loops generated by transcription-replication collisions. This is the one step in the chain that has been shown to separate AOA2 from ALS4 at the molecular level: AOA2 alleles abolish both the sumoylation and the Rrp45 interaction, while ALS4 alleles leave them intact.

evidence.reference_title: SETX sumoylation: A link between DNA damage and RNA surveillance disrupted in AOA2.
evidence.snippet: Importantly, we showed that AOA2 but not ALS4 mutations prevented both SETX sumoylation and the Rrp45 interaction.

evidence.reference_title: SETX sumoylation: A link between DNA damage and RNA surveillance disrupted in AOA2.
evidence.snippet: We suggest that SETX links transcription, DNA damage and RNA surveillance, and discuss here how this link can be relevant to AOA2 disease.

nodes.description: Wasting of distal limb muscles, following the motor component of the axonal neuropathy; in some families it is prominent enough to resemble a distal motor neuronopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in senataxin responsible for Quebec cluster of ataxia with neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: All cases have a homogeneous phenotype consisting of a progressive ataxia appearing between 2 and 20 (mean age, 14.8) years of age with associated dysarthria, saccadic ocular pursuit, distal amyotrophy, sensory and motor neuropathy, and increased alpha-fetoprotein levels but absence of oculomotor apraxia.

nodes.description: Scanning, slurred cerebellar speech, present in almost all patients.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: two pedigree studies and a comprehensive review.
evidence.snippet: Key clinical features included ataxia (100%), dysarthria (99.2%), cerebellar atrophy (99.4%), and elevated AFP (97.6%).

nodes.description: A second, non-neurological consequence of losing senataxin, worked out in the knockout mouse: programmed meiotic double-strand breaks persist, Rad51 filaments fail to disassemble, R-loops accumulate, crossing-over fails, and meiotic sex chromosome inactivation is incomplete.
nodes.id: Failure of Meiotic Recombination and Sex Chromosome Inactivation

animal_models.description: Reproduces the meiotic phenotype in full, and it is where the mechanism was originally worked out; the human testicular histology was subsequently matched to it.
animal_models.genotype: Setx knockout (Setx-/-, Cre-LoxP deletion of exon 4)
animal_models.name: Setx knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Senataxin plays an essential role with DNA damage response proteins in meiotic recombination and gene silencing.
evidence.snippet: Disruption of the Setx gene caused persistence of DNA double-strand breaks, a defect in disassembly of Rad51 filaments, accumulation of DNA:RNA hybrids (R-loops), and ultimately a failure of crossing-over.

nodes.description: Gait ataxia is the presenting sign in almost every patient; the recorded exceptions presented with head tremor and with writer's cramp.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: a clinical and genetic study of 19 patients.
evidence.snippet: The initial sign was gait ataxia in all but two patients who presented with head tremor and writer cramp, respectively.

nodes.description: In the one AOA2 patient whose testis has been examined histologically, seminiferous tubules contained spermatogonia and primary spermatocytes but no spermatids — the same pachytene-stage arrest described in the mouse. Sperm production was impaired in all three patients in whom it was assessed.

evidence.reference_title: Germ cell arrest associated with aSETX mutation in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: In accordance with the murine phenotype, testis histology revealed disrupted seminiferous tubules with spermatogonia and primary spermatocytes, but absent spermatids.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of Spermatogenesis and Infertility in Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2 (AOA2).
evidence.snippet: Analyses of testicular biopsies from an AOA2 patient recapitulate features of the histology seen in Setx-knockout mice, strongly suggesting an underlying mechanism centering on DNA-damage-mediated germ cell apoptosis.

nodes.description: Raised total cholesterol is reported in individual patients and is the reason GeneReviews advises a low-cholesterol diet. Unlike AOA1, where hypercholesterolaemia and hypoalbuminaemia are near-constant markers, in AOA2 it is inconsistent — one reviewed patient had normal albumin, total cholesterol and immunoglobulins.

evidence.reference_title: Delayed diagnosis of ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2 in a Peruvian patient, a case report.
evidence.snippet: Laboratory tests showed elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein levels and increased total cholesterol.

nodes.description: AOA2 patient fibroblasts and lymphoblasts carry constitutive oxidative DNA damage and are hypersensitive to hydrogen peroxide, camptothecin and mitomycin C but not to ionizing radiation. The selectivity matters: it separates AOA2 from ataxia-telangiectasia, whose cells are radiosensitive, and it points at lesions arising during transcription and replication rather than at a general break-repair failure. Complementation with full-length SETX cDNA rescues the sensitivity, so the defect is senataxin's.

evidence.reference_title: Senataxin, defective in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2, is involved in the defense against oxidative DNA damage.
evidence.snippet: AOA2 cells are sensitive to H2O2, camptothecin, and mitomycin C, but not to ionizing radiation, and sensitivity was rescued with full-length SETX cDNA.

evidence.reference_title: Senataxin, defective in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2, is involved in the defense against oxidative DNA damage.
evidence.snippet: AOA2 cells exhibited constitutive oxidative DNA damage and enhanced chromosomal instability in response to H2O2.

nodes.description: Saccadic hypometria with a staircase pattern of corrective saccades. Oculographic study argues that this, rather than the presence of head thrusts, is the reliable sign of oculomotor apraxia in AOA2.

evidence.reference_title: Saccades and eye-head coordination in ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: The most salient deficit of the patients was saccadic hypometria with a typical staircase pattern.

evidence.reference_title: Saccades and eye-head coordination in ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: Our study emphasises that in AOA2, hypometric saccades with a staircase pattern are a more reliable sign of oculomotor apraxia than head thrust movements.

nodes.description: Senataxin depletion changes the transcription of autophagy and lysosomal-degradation genes, apparently through direct recruitment of RNA polymerase II to those genes rather than through a downstream signalling route.
nodes.id: Impaired Transcriptional Control of Autophagy Genes

nodes.description: Large-fibre sensory loss, consistent with the depletion of large myelinated fibres seen on sural nerve biopsy.

evidence.reference_title: Sensory neuronopathy in ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: A 40 year-old woman, born to consanguineous parents, presented with ataxia, decreased vibration sense, areflexia, indifferent plantar responses, preserved muscle volume and strength, and oculomotor apraxia; elevated levels of serum alpha-fetoprotein and creatine-kinase were found.

nodes.description: Senataxin is a nucleoplasmic superfamily-I DNA/RNA helicase homologous to yeast Sen1p, with a C-terminal helicase domain and an N-terminal protein-interaction domain. With the protein truncated or inactive, the cell loses a single enzyme that is used in several places at once: unwinding R-loops behind paused polymerase, unwinding them again where transcription meets replication, and docking the transcription machinery to RNA-processing and damage-response partners.
nodes.id: Loss of Senataxin RNA/DNA Helicase Activity

evidence.reference_title: Senataxin, defective in ataxia oculomotor apraxia type 2, is involved in the defense against oxidative DNA damage.
evidence.snippet: We report that senataxin, defective in ataxia oculomotor apraxia (AOA) type 2, is a nuclear protein involved in the DNA damage response.

evidence.reference_title: Senataxin, defective in the neurodegenerative disorder ataxia with oculomotor apraxia 2, lies at the interface of transcription and the DNA damage response.
evidence.snippet: These results indicate that senataxin localizes to sites of collision between components of the replisome and the transcription apparatus and that it is targeted to R loops, where it plays an important role at the interface of transcription and the DNA damage response.

nodes.description: Wheelchair dependence follows onset by roughly fifteen years on pooled review, and by about twenty years in one cohort. Age at onset does not predict how fast this happens.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: two pedigree studies and a comprehensive review.
evidence.snippet: Disease progression to wheelchair dependence averaged 15.9 ± 8.6 years, with no significant differences observed in gender or adult onset and juvenile onset.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: a clinical and genetic study of 19 patients.
evidence.snippet: Mean disease duration until wheelchair was around 20 years.

nodes.description: Advised by GeneReviews as prevention of secondary complications. Note the evidence for it is a management recommendation rather than a trial, and hypercholesterolaemia is inconsistent in AOA2.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2.
evidence.snippet: Preventions of secondary complications: A low-cholesterol diet is advised. Surveillance: Routine follow up with a neurologist.

nodes.description: Impaired sperm production, with a testicular histology showing arrest at the primary spermatocyte stage. Assessed in only three patients so far, but impaired in all three.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of Spermatogenesis and Infertility in Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2 (AOA2).
evidence.snippet: Sperm production was impaired in all patients assessed (3/3, 100%).

nodes.description: Difficulty initiating voluntary horizontal saccades, classically with compensatory head thrusts. Despite naming the disease it is the least consistent of its cardinal features: cohort estimates range from 32% to 56%, and two series describe patients with none at all.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: clinical, biological and genotype/phenotype correlation study of a cohort of 90 patients.
evidence.snippet: Polyneuropathy was found in 97.5% of AOA2 patients, cerebellar atrophy in 96%, occasional oculomotor apraxia in 51%, pyramidal signs in 20.5%, head tremor in 14%, dystonia in 13.5%, strabismus in 12.3% and chorea in 9.5%.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: two pedigree studies and a comprehensive review.
evidence.snippet: Oculomotor apraxia was observed in 34.2% of cases.

evidence.reference_title: SETX mutations are a frequent genetic cause of juvenile and adult onset cerebellar ataxia with neuropathy and elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein.
evidence.snippet: None had obvious oculomotor apraxia at the latest examination (age 14-45 years).

nodes.description: Rehabilitation aimed at the disability produced by the peripheral neuropathy. It is symptomatic and compensatory; there is no disease-modifying treatment for AOA2.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2.
evidence.snippet: Treatment of manifestations: Physical therapy for disabilities resulting from peripheral neuropathy; wheelchair for mobility as needed; educational support (e.g., computer with speech recognition and special keyboard for typing) to compensate for difficulties in reading (caused by oculomotor apraxia) and in writing (caused by upper-limb ataxia).

nodes.description: The defining manifestation: a slowly progressive cerebellar syndrome with truncal and limb ataxia. It is present in essentially every reported patient.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: two pedigree studies and a comprehensive review.
evidence.snippet: Key clinical features included ataxia (100%), dysarthria (99.2%), cerebellar atrophy (99.4%), and elevated AFP (97.6%).

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2 caused by a novel homozygous mutation in SETX gene, and literature review.
evidence.snippet: The main clinical features were cerebellar ataxia (100%), peripheral neuropathy (94.6%), cerebellar atrophy (95.3%) and elevated AFP concentration (92.0%).

nodes.description: Loss of Purkinje cells from the cerebellar cortex is the neuropathological endpoint of the cerebellar arm. Post-mortem material in AOA2 is scarce; the claim rests on a small number of autopsied patients and on the imaging correlate.
nodes.id: Purkinje Cell Degeneration in the Cerebellar Cortex

animal_models.description: Complete loss of Setx in the mouse produces no cerebellar degeneration and no ataxia, so the model cannot be used to study the neurodegenerative arm of AOA2.
animal_models.genotype: Setx knockout (Setx-/-, Cre-LoxP deletion of exon 4)
animal_models.name: Setx knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of Spermatogenesis and Infertility in Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2 (AOA2).
evidence.snippet: The major clinical features of AOA2 include onset in the second decade, progressive cerebellar ataxia with axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy, diffuse cerebellar atrophy, frequent oculomotor apraxia, early loss of reflexes, loss of Purkinje cells in the cerebellar cortex, and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) serum level

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: a clinical, pathologic, and genetic study.
evidence.snippet: Postmortem findings are also reported in one of the patients.

nodes.description: Broken-up smooth pursuit, described as a constant feature in the French-Canadian founder cohort and confirmed by video-oculography across the oculomotor-apraxia ataxias.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in senataxin responsible for Quebec cluster of ataxia with neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: All cases have a homogeneous phenotype consisting of a progressive ataxia appearing between 2 and 20 (mean age, 14.8) years of age with associated dysarthria, saccadic ocular pursuit, distal amyotrophy, sensory and motor neuropathy, and increased alpha-fetoprotein levels but absence of oculomotor apraxia.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2: clinical, biological and genotype/phenotype correlation study of a cohort of 90 patients.
evidence.snippet: The probability of missing AOA2 diagnosis, in case of sequencing senataxin gene only in non-Friedreich ataxia non-ataxia-telangiectasia ataxic patients with AFP level > or =7 microg/l, is 0.23% and the probability for a non-Friedreich ataxia non-ataxia-telangiectasia ataxic patient to be affected with AOA2 with AFP levels > or =7 microg/l is 46%.

evidence.reference_title: Comparing ataxias with oculomotor apraxia: a multimodal study of AOA1, AOA2 and AT focusing on video-oculography and alpha-fetoprotein.
evidence.snippet: Specific distinctive alpha-fetoprotein thresholds were determined for AOA1 (7-15 µg/L), AOA2 (15-65 µg/L) and AT (>65 µg/L).

evidence.reference_title: Is high AFP associated with liver diseases in ataxia-telangiectasia and ataxia-oculomotor apraxia?
evidence.snippet: While 69% (9/13) of AT patients had elevated liver enzymes and 56% (5/9) had abnormal liver imaging, both were normal in all AOA2 patients.

readouts.interpretation: An AFP above the 7 microg/l threshold in an ataxic patient is what selects SETX for sequencing. The link is empirical: no mechanism connecting senataxin loss to AFP production has been established, so this is recorded as a correlation with the genetic lesion rather than as a readout of any modelled mechanism node.

meta.specificity: Shared with ataxia-telangiectasia and, at lower levels, AOA1; the concentration bands differ between the three.

nodes.description: The only published constitutive Setx-null mouse. It is a good model of the meiotic arm of senataxin function and not a model of the disease: the animals are male-infertile with a pachytene-stage block, and they have no ataxia, no cerebellar degeneration and no Purkinje cell loss.

evidence.reference_title: Senataxin plays an essential role with DNA damage response proteins in meiotic recombination and gene silencing.
evidence.snippet: Senataxin, mutated in the human genetic disorder ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2 (AOA2), plays an important role in maintaining genome integrity by coordination of transcription, DNA replication, and the DNA damage response.

nodes.description: Wheelchair use becomes necessary a median of about fifteen years after onset. Recorded as a rehabilitation action carrying the device as a qualifier, since the NCIT wheelchair concept is a device rather than a clinical action.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with Oculomotor Apraxia Type 2.
evidence.snippet: Treatment of manifestations: Physical therapy for disabilities resulting from peripheral neuropathy; wheelchair for mobility as needed; educational support (e.g., computer with speech recognition and special keyboard for typing) to compensate for difficulties in reading (caused by oculomotor apraxia) and in writing (caused by upper-limb ataxia).
